disposition: capsaicin occurs in cited comparator papers
assessment: The study administered intrarectal allyl isothiocyanate and assessed nociception. Capsaicin appears in cited studies of a receptor and experimental colitis. No ground cayenne exposure or Parkinson pain score is reported.

disposition: isolated irritant and cited knockout phenotype
assessment: The article uses allyl isothiocyanate rather than ground mustard seed. Its depression-like discussion describes a prior study of peptide-YY knockout mice. Depression was not measured in this pain experiment.

The original used peanut oil as an ungraded intrarectal vehicle and measured freezing, grimace and mechanical pain outcomes. The oil group in wild-type mice had a higher hindpaw threshold than its own baseline. The design does not isolate orally consumed refined oil. Related assessment PMID28106168 already records the key comparison.

disposition: vehicle and discussion of earlier depression-like phenotype
assessment: Peanut oil was an ungraded intrarectal pain-test vehicle. Depression-like behavior is cited for the knockout phenotype and is not an outcome after oil treatment.
